scope: first successful partial decryption of a real gamestate

decrypt.key_formula: challenge ^ seq (seq = packet first 4 bytes, signed int)
decrypt.command: empty (so the key should be constant)

interpretation.partial_success: the map name mp_cross_fire and the gametype prefix decode correctly, proving the key formula challenge ^ seq is right
interpretation.why_the_first_bytes_are_noise: the leading 10 bytes decode to 3f3db53bb53b3f3f3f3f instead of 07 00000000 01000000..., so either the key is not constant over the first few bytes (a non-empty command string we have not located) or our command-string offset is wrong and the real lastClientCommandString still advances the key early on
interpretation.note: later bytes decode as clean ASCII, so the cipher implementation and the challenge value are both correct

what_we_gained: proof that decrypting a live 2697 gamestate is possible with data we can read
the real text 'mp_cross_fire' inside a gamestate - the exact configstring the client needs
the plaintext layout shows a 4-byte zero field followed by the map name, then 'mp', then binary
next: locate the true lastClientCommandString by scanning client_t for an ASCII string after name+265420..266500 instead of trusting the computed 265480
re-decrypt and require the header to decode to 07 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00
then extract the full configstring set from the plaintext and mirror it in server1649370
